description.summary: privileged shell protocol for the Huginn compositor

protocol.description:
The contract between the Huginn compositor and the desktop software around it — a bar, a settings page, a screen-layout tool.
This protocol covers only what no standard protocol provides. Panels, the dock and the wallpaper are wlr-layer-shell surfaces; the lock screen is ext-session-lock-v1. Do not duplicate those here.
The compositor should only advertise this global to clients it considers privileged. Huginn does not yet enforce that, which is tracked as a gap rather than a design decision.
Stability: additive changes only. Add requests and events and bump the interface version; never change or remove an existing one. Keeping to that is what makes moving this file to its own repository a mechanical step.

interface.name: raven_shell_manager_v1

description.summary: entry point for the desktop shell

interface.description: Handed to the shell so it can observe compositor state it cannot see as an ordinary Wayland client.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: release the manager

request.description: Objects created through this manager are unaffected and must be destroyed separately.

request.name: get_workspace_state

description.summary: observe workspace state

request.description:
Create an object reporting how many workspaces exist, which one is active, and which hold windows, so a panel can render indicators.
The compositor sends one state event immediately on creation, so a client never has to render a placeholder while it waits.

request.name: open_quick_settings

description.summary: open the compositor-drawn quick settings panel

request.description:
Open the quick settings panel, exactly as the keybinding would. The panel is drawn by the compositor, so a bar that wants a click on its battery to lead somewhere has to ask for it here; it has no surface of its own to show.
A no-op if the panel is already open, and while the session is locked: nothing resolves under the lock screen, and a request from a client is not an exception to that.

request.name: get_output_layout

description.summary: observe and arrange the screens

request.description:
Create an object reporting every connected screen with its place in the desktop, through which a client can move screens and set their scale. The arrangement is remembered by the compositor across sessions, by connector name.
The compositor sends the full set of output events followed by done immediately on creation, and again whenever the set of screens or their geometry changes.

request.name: capture_output

description.summary: capture a whole screen

request.description: Create a capture of the screen with this connector name, as reported by raven_output_layout_v1.output. A name that matches no connected screen creates a capture that is already stopped: its first and only event is stopped.

request.name: capture_window

description.summary: capture one window

request.description:
Create a capture of the window whose ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 identifier is 'identifier'. The capture is the window alone, with the decorations the compositor draws for it and nothing that overlaps it, at the density of the screen it is on. It follows the window as it moves and resizes (a resize is a new buffer_size), and while the window is off screen — minimized, put away, on a workspace no screen shows — no frames are delivered until it is back.
An identifier that names no window creates a capture whose first and only event is stopped.

request.name: capture_region

description.summary: capture a rectangle of one screen

request.description: Create a capture of a rectangle of the named screen, in logical pixels relative to that screen's top-left corner, as raven_region_selection_v1.selected reports one. The rectangle is clipped to the screen; one that is empty after clipping, or a name that matches no screen, creates a capture whose first and only event is stopped.

request.name: select_region

description.summary: let the user drag out a rectangle

request.description: Put up the compositor's own region selection — the one Shift+Print uses — and report what the user drags out. Escape cancels it. Only one selection is up at a time: asking while one is already up, or while the session is locked, cancels the new one at once.

interface.name: raven_output_layout_v1

description.summary: where each screen sits, and the means to move it

interface.description:
Created through raven_shell_manager_v1.get_output_layout.
Positions are in the desktop's logical pixels, shared by every screen. Changes are staged with set_position and set_scale and take effect on apply, together, so a client arranging three screens does not have the desktop reflow three times. Whatever is applied is saved and reapplied the next time a screen of that name connects.

description.summary: stop observing the layout

request.name: set_position

description.summary: stage a position for a screen

request.description: Where the screen's top-left corner should go. A position that would overlap another screen is pushed right of it when applied, and the whole arrangement is shifted so its top-left is the origin; the geometry reported afterwards is the truth.

arg.name: name
arg.summary: connector name, as reported by output

request.name: set_scale

description.summary: stage a scale for a screen

request.description: The effective scale to lay the screen out at, overriding the one the compositor derives from its physical size. Zero returns it to the derived scale. Clients are still told an integer scale; see the compositor's documentation on scaling.

request.name: apply

description.summary: apply and save the staged changes

request.description: Apply every staged change at once, save the result, and report the new geometry through output events followed by done. A name that matches no connected screen is saved for when it connects.

event.name: output

description.summary: one screen

event.description: Sent for every screen, followed by done. Sent again for all of them whenever any changes.

arg.name: mm_width
arg.summary: panel width in millimetres, 0 if unknown

arg.name: mm_height
arg.summary: panel height in millimetres, 0 if unknown

arg.name: focused
arg.summary: 1 if this is the focused screen

description.summary: the set of output events is complete
workspace count, active index and occupancy
stop observing workspace state

request.name: activate

description.summary: switch to a workspace

request.description:
Ask the compositor to make workspace 'index' active.
An out-of-range index is ignored rather than clamped: clamping would turn a shell bug into a silent jump to an unrelated workspace, which is harder to notice than nothing happening.

event.name: state

description.summary: workspace state changed

event.description: Sent once when this object is created, and again whenever any field changes. The compositor does not send this event if nothing changed.

arg.name: active
arg.summary: zero-based index of the active workspace

arg.name: occupied
arg.summary: bitmask; bit N is set if workspace N holds at least one window. Caps at 32 workspaces, which is well beyond any sane count

interface.name: raven_capture_v1

description.summary: frames of a screen, a window or a region

interface.description:
Created through the capture requests of raven_shell_manager_v1.
The client supplies the memory: it creates a wl_shm buffer of the size buffer_size last announced, in format argb8888 or xrgb8888 with a stride of at least four bytes a pixel, and hands it over with frame. The compositor draws the source into it and answers ready, or failed. A capture never delivers a frame the client did not ask for, so the client sets the frame rate by how often it asks.
Frames are drawn only when the source has changed since the last one this capture delivered. A still desktop asked for a frame keeps the request pending until something moves; the first request is always answered straight away.
While any capture is delivering frames the compositor shows its recording indicator on the screens involved, and while the session is locked no capture delivers anything: a pending frame waits for the unlock.

entry.name: clicks
entry.summary: draw a fading ring where the pointer is pressed, into frames only, never onto the screen

entry.name: already_pending
entry.summary: frame while another frame is pending

request.name: destroy

description.summary: stop capturing

request.description: A pending frame is abandoned; its buffer is the client's again.

request.name: frame

description.summary: draw the next frame into this buffer

request.description:
Ask for the next frame. Exactly one of ready and failed answers it. Asking again before that answer is the already_pending error.
A buffer that is not wl_shm, is not argb8888 or xrgb8888, or is not the size of the last buffer_size, is answered with failed.

event.name: buffer_size

description.summary: the size frames are drawn at

event.description: The size in physical pixels a buffer must have. Sent before any other event, and again whenever the source changes size; a frame pending at that moment is answered with failed, since its buffer is now the wrong size.

event.name: ready

description.summary: the buffer holds a frame

event.description: The buffer from the last frame request now holds the source as it was drawn at this CLOCK_MONOTONIC time, and is the client's again.

event.name: failed

description.summary: the buffer was not filled

event.description: The last frame request could not be answered with this buffer. If a buffer_size came just before, allocate a buffer of that size and ask again; otherwise the buffer itself was unusable.

event.name: stopped

description.summary: the source is gone

event.description: The screen was unplugged, the window closed, or the source never existed. A pending frame is answered with failed first. Nothing more is sent; destroy the object.

interface.name: raven_region_selection_v1

description.summary: a rectangle the user drags out

interface.description: Created through raven_shell_manager_v1.select_region. Exactly one of selected and cancelled is sent, and then nothing else.

description.summary: release the selection, taking it down if it is still up

event.name: selected

description.summary: the user finished dragging

event.description: In logical pixels, relative to the top-left corner of the screen named, which is the screen the drag started on.

description.summary: Escape, or the selection could not be put up
